text: Skillset is a wrapper around Vercel's Skills CLI that installs a predefined list of skills at once. npm install -g @itsmeyaw/skillset Or run without installing: npx @itsmeyaw/skillset --help . Build your own Skillset once, then reuse it in every project. Run commands without arguments and Skillset prompts you for everything. 1. Create your Skillset. --set my-set names a Skillset that you can use in all your projects: skillset add --set my-set You are asked for: Run it again with another source to mix skills from several repos into the same Skillset. skillset ls --set my-set shows what is in it. 2. Use it in any project. From each project that should receive the skills: cd ~ /projects/some-project skillset install my-set You are asked which skills, which agents, project or global scope, and symlink or copy, then to confirm. 3. Keep it fresh. Skills are pinned to commits, so nothing changes until you update: skillset update --set my-set # move pins to the latest commits skillset rm --set my-set # pick skills to drop Re-run skillset install my-set in a project to pick up the changes. Skills outside the Skillset are never removed. Installs are recorded in skills-lock.json . Every prompt has a flag, so the same steps work in scripts; see Commands . Prefer a Skillset that lives in a repo so teammates share it? Omit --set to use ./skillset.json and commit it. See User Skillsets . Every command accepts --set <value> (default ./skillset.json ) and --help . add and install <source> create the file if it is missing. Quote sources containing # in your shell. Private repositories use your existing Git credentials. Local paths and direct downloads cannot be pinned. Pass a bare name to --set to keep a Skillset outside any project, so every project can use it: skillset add mattpocock/skills -s grilling --set my-set skillset install my-set skillset ls -g # list your User Skillsets They are stored in the first of $SKILLSET_HOME , $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/skillset , or ~/.skillset . To use a file in the current directory, give a path ending in .json . { "$schema" : " https://raw.githubusercontent.com/itsmeyaw/skillset/main/schemas/skillset/v1.json " , "skills" : [ { "name" : " grilling " , "source" : " mattpocock/skills " , "commit" : " 5863806dd4e15c63174bee4e7515a4256792ecfa " } ] } You can use the JSON Schema for editor validation. Skillset collects no data itself. However, Vercel's Skills CLI library sends anonymous usage telemetry by default. See what is collected . To turn it off, set DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1 or DO_NOT_TRACK=1 : DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1 skillset install my-set License This project is licensed under the MIT
